claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from severe performance issues and heavy stuttering after moving to Unreal Engine 5.

citations.review_text: I haven't played much since I got it. But recently I wanted to try the CodZ maps ported into Pavlov. The performance is terrible. I have a Ryzen 5 3600XT, RTX 3060 12gb, 32gb of DDR4, and the game is installed on an Gen 4 NVMe. My game has unplayable stuttering that makes me sick after a just few minutes.

I bought this a few years ago on sale because I knew I wanted to play it when I got PCVR headset. Anyways fast foward to now when I finally got to play it and found out that first of all the original mods are gone and second of all they ''upgraded" the game engine to Unreal Engine 5 which is causing a lot of stuttering (I have an RX6800, every other VR game runs good). The player base is also dwindling in numbers. Not worth getting in 2025. I would recommend Contractors instead because it actually has lots of good mods and no performance issues.

Disappointing Performance and Accessibility Issues

I was really looking forward to trying Pavlov VR, but unfortunately the performance issues made it hard to enjoy.
Even with an RTX 3070 and a Ryzen 9 3950X, the game runs very poorly — with frequent stutters and inconsistent frame rates. It feels heavily unoptimized for what it offers.

The tutorial does an okay job at teaching the basics like movement and shooting, but it doesn’t go much deeper.
I also struggled to find a way back to the main menu — after several minutes of searching, the only solution I found was to close and restart the game.

Because of these problems, I didn’t even make it to the multiplayer part, which was the main reason I bought the game. Hopefully future updates will improve the performance and usability, because it seems like there’s potential underneath all the technical issues.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game lacks proper gunstock calibration options, making it difficult for players using physical gunstocks.

citations.review_text:
Total Technical Disaster. A Heartbreaking Mess

I am genuinely baffled by how a game can be released in such an abysmal state. Even with a high-end setup (Ryzen 7 and RTX 5080), I wasted two agonizing hours just trying to get it to run without constant stuttering on Quest 3. The Steam VR integration is fundamentally broken.

To make matters worse, proper gunstock calibration is non-existent. The options available at the shooting range are utterly useless and don't allow for any meaningful adjustment. As a result, the game is completely unplayable for anyone with a physical gunstock.

This isn't just a lack of polish; it's a total failure of optimization. It breaks my heart that I’m past the two-week refund window because this feels like a complete waste of money. Do yourself a favor and stay far away from this nightmare.

Pavlov used to be one of the best VR shooters available. At its peak, it felt like the closest thing we had to CS:GO in VR: focused, competitive, simple, and genuinely fun.

That version of the game is basically gone.

The current game feels scattered between too many modes, custom content, and community-server gimmicks. Instead of strengthening the core shooter experience, Pavlov became a fragmented mod playground where the active playerbase feels split across whatever random mode is populated that day — usually TTT or other casual lobbies. If you are looking for a serious VR tactical shooter, this is no longer the first game I would recommend.

The numbers do not help its case either. SteamDB currently shows Pavlov sitting around 127 players, with a 24-hour peak of 154, compared to its all-time peak of 3,221 back in January 2021. That is a brutal falloff for a multiplayer-only VR shooter. Steam also shows recent reviews as Mixed, despite the older lifetime score still being positive.

The mod situation also did not help. Update 29 retired Steam Workshop support, moved content delivery to mod.io, and made older custom content incompatible unless it was updated. The developers framed it as part of the engine upgrade and cross-platform future-proofing, but from a player perspective, it felt like a hard reset that damaged a lot of the community content people actually cared about.

Pavlov should have stayed focused: a strong CS-style VR shooter with a handful of polished modes and maps. Instead, it spread itself thin, divided the playerbase, and lost what made it special.

There are better VR shooters now for almost every individual thing Pavlov tries to do.

Not recommended.

Honestly, if you’re looking for that CS-style experience in VR now, you’re better off elsewhere. Just go play Breachers. Yeah, it leans more toward Siege than classic CS, but it’s one of the only solid defuse-style shooters left in VR right now. 

Or you could try Vail… but let’s be real.

As much as I would like to give this game a positive review, there are currently too many issues holding it back for me to fully recommend it.

First are the good things 

The weapon handling, gunplay, and game modes are some of the best you can find in VR. Whenever I don't have anything else to play, I often come back to Pavlov because playing with friends can be one of the most fun experiences in gaming. You get to meet people from all over the world and have genuinely social experiences.

TTT is one of the most creative game modes I have ever played. It is a unique experience that can keep players entertained for hundreds of hours. The game also runs very well and is highly optimized.

Now for the problems.

The biggest issue is the current player base. There simply aren't enough active lobbies anymore. Many modded servers are completely empty, and you might only find around 10 to 15 active servers, with many of them having no players. Because of this, a lot of the game's mods and custom content are rarely used.

Another issue is the community atmosphere. While Pavlov can be incredibly fun and social, some lobbies can also be very toxic, which can drive new players away. The game has a lot of potential with its custom content, but many mods are either unused or lack the player base needed to keep them alive.

And as Mhx Air said in his steam review, and i Quote

 "Dead game. The switch to UE5 literally killed the whole game and community. All the best mods were on Legacy, and they removed Legacy. The devs should have just made a sequel instead of rugpulling us and forcing us to have an update that nobody wanted. From thousands of players to less than 100. Look at Steam charts. They should have never forced us to switch to UE5. I just wanna play my Workshop mods again bro. I don't care about UE5 graphics or the Jared coins microtransaction slop. Bring back Legacy. Many of us genuinely feel scammed, and left nostalgic for the good old days.""

Overall, Pavlov is a …

Reasons for the Decline in PC Player Count
Broken Mod Support: A significant factor was the shift from the highly popular and easy-to-use Steam Workshop to the less intuitive Mod.io platform as part of a major engine upgrade (to Unreal Engine 5). This change made it difficult for content creators to port or develop new maps and mods (such as popular Call of Duty zombie maps), which had previously been a major draw for the game.
Developer Focus on Console: Many PC players feel the developers, Vankrupt Games, abandoned the PC version to focus on the more lucrative Quest and PSVR2 platforms. The PC version allegedly lagged in features for a long time, leading to player frustration.
Technical Issues and Performance: The engine upgrade itself caused numerous problems for PC players, including performance drops, input issues, and controller problems, some of which were never adequately addressed for all users. The game became harder to run for some players, prompting them to leave.
Gameplay Changes: The update also introduced unwanted gameplay changes, such as a forced HUD showing teammate locations through walls, which altered the tactical flow of popular modes like "Push" and "Search and Destroy".
Competition: Due to these issues, many players migrated to alternative VR shooters like Contractors or Ghosts of Tabor, which maintained better mod support or offered a more stable experience.    TY for killing…

The issue with doing that to a game that's been out for a while is that a lot of the modders aren't actively keeping things up to date, so we lost all the COD zombie maps and have only gotten 1 or two back a WHILE later after some dedicated modders revived them.

So in short, the devs attempt to shore up the game is the very thing that ended up breaking everything good about it, which has led to an exodus of the playerbase. At this point, its maybe one or two populated servers, and then a ton of private lobbies and empty lobbies. And sadly, I can't blame them. Keep in mind, this game made the move to UE 5 in summer of 2023. Plenty of time to fix it up for the modding community, so this is not just a matter of impatience but an active decision to stall / not consider it.

Since the update, i've installed the game twice in the last year to see where it's at, and sadly it seems mostly everything has stopped dead in Feb. No new mods really, no new dev updates, no new mod kit expansions to allow for the people still playing to save it. Save your money and just accept that you missed out on this title when it was king, and if you pick it up now it will be a shell of it's former self.

citations.review_text: The creators had essentially made Garry's Mod VR. Lots of community maps, gamemodes, etc. It was the only unique thing about this game. They then decided to do crossplay with Playstation VR and ruined the entire modding aspect of this game, which again, was the only thing this game had going for it. Onward was a better shooter (before they also sold out to PSVR) and Contractors offered better gamemodes and weapon customization. All Pavlov had was the community content. I hope Sony gave them a huge payout for the downgrades they performed to make it PSVR compatible, because this game is worthless now. I am beyond surprised that they don't at least provide an option for PC players to revert to the old engine that had all the mod support, because leaving behind this kind of reputation is what kills these smaller studios. A lack of trust will kill the sales of any future games they make.

This was once the best multiplayer online shooter VR game on Steam, bar none. The controls, gun audio, and player activity were all top-tier. But ever since the developers started considering cross-play with PSVR players, while being unable to resolve Sony's ban on mod loading, and migrated from the Steam Workshop to mod.io, they lost a huge number of map creators and players. The development team stopped listening to player feedback, shifting more of their focus to mobile development for short-term gains. With PC updates and optimizations nearly abandoned, it’s not just veteran players feeling disappointed and leaving—it’s also the developers giving up on the game themselves.

This game used to be the best VR game out there. Since they updated the game back in 2024/2025 and introduced cross platform with PSVR and PCVR the game was ruined. They changed the way downloading mods work from steam workshop to an in-game mod list, which on paper seems like it would be better, but it's not. Over 70% of the previous maps were never ported over. Custom gamemodes like prison break and SCP containment are no longer around because of the lack of custom server/gamemode support. Gameplay is still smooth tho, but their new community guidelines because of Playstation makes the game incredibly unfun.

This is the most heartbreaking review. I can't believe that I don't recommend this game, because it used to be my favorite. But it is no longer that way. Here's why:

I played this game in 2021-23, and it used to be THE BEST VR GAME. But dev team did everything to kill PC community. First - crossplay with console "people", second - they shifted focus on standalone game that runs on headset (basically mobile version that's just bad compared to PC). AND the last nail in the coffin was transition to new UE version that WIPED all custom maps, gamemods and basically all community work that players did. Devs thought that if they give time to modders to update ALL mods to new UE - modders will do it. It was not the case. Nobody wants to do the same job twice, this is just not how it works. The irony of that UE update is that I haven't noticed any changes to the game AT ALL. It's just the same graphics, physics, same everything. The only thing that changed is that we no longer have CUSTOM game mods, which was the most fun part. Now we only have classic CS maps and TTT. And whole bunch of empty servers. Oh! They added SKINS! WOW! Totally worth it. 

If you are a game dev team member who wants to make a new VR game. Just copy this game and make it slightly better. You will win the market. This game used to have so much potential, but it all went down the drain. I mean, how? It was a NEARLY PERFECT game! Solid 9/10. Best VR game on the market. I mean seriously, if somebody just make the same game, with lobbies and no matchmaking. With focus on community made mods and maps. WOULDN'T EVER break community mods with useless updates. And just focus on PC only, no console and standalone crap. This would be a #1 VR shooter game. Please, we need a new game like this.

This was a "home" a perfect game with countless polished fun mods and maps. This game was valued because it gave an option for the players to create their own game and content.  The developer either didnt understand it or didnt care. They destroyed their game by changing an engine for the crossplay. It didnt help with online at all. But it killed the game completely for everyone on PC. I believe the lost about 8 000 000 $ or more of mods and maps, something that they personally would never have the budget for.

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the gunplay, weapon handling, and reload mechanics.

citations.review_text:
As much as I would like to give this game a positive review, there are currently too many issues holding it back for me to fully recommend it.

First are the good things 

The weapon handling, gunplay, and game modes are some of the best you can find in VR. Whenever I don't have anything else to play, I often come back to Pavlov because playing with friends can be one of the most fun experiences in gaming. You get to meet people from all over the world and have genuinely social experiences.

TTT is one of the most creative game modes I have ever played. It is a unique experience that can keep players entertained for hundreds of hours. The game also runs very well and is highly optimized.

Now for the problems.

The biggest issue is the current player base. There simply aren't enough active lobbies anymore. Many modded servers are completely empty, and you might only find around 10 to 15 active servers, with many of them having no players. Because of this, a lot of the game's mods and custom content are rarely used.

Another issue is the community atmosphere. While Pavlov can be incredibly fun and social, some lobbies can also be very toxic, which can drive new players away. The game has a lot of potential with its custom content, but many mods are either unused or lack the player base needed to keep them alive.

And as Mhx Air said in his steam review, and i Quote

 "Dead game. The switch to UE5 literally killed the whole game and community. All the best mods were on Legacy, and they removed Legacy. The devs should have just made a sequel instead of rugpulling us and forcing us to have an update that nobody wanted. From thousands of players to less than 100. Look at Steam charts. They should have never forced us to switch to UE5. I just wanna play my Workshop mods again bro. I don't care about UE5 graphics or the Jared coins microtransaction slop. Bring back Legacy. Many of us genuinely feel scammed, and left nostalgic for the good old days.""

Overall, Pavlov is a …

Wish I could still play this on my Meta Quest 2 through VirtualDesktop/SteamVR. I loved the arcade-y feel it had compared to Contractors (which I feel was more inspired by Call of Duty). Contractors had the better physics, but Pavlov felt better shooting the guns imo. 277 hours played of this early access game, just for the developers to completely change/overhaul the engine on the 1.0 release, making it impossible for me to play it on my meta quest 2 through Virtual Desktop and SteamVR. Had to use the Oculus AirLink instead, which my internet is not able to handle. So now this great game has been gathering virtual dust since its official release date.

There is Pavlov Shack, which is a lighter version of this game that's on the Meta store. Less populated lobbies and smaller maps, but still really fun. I had to purchase that for $20 since I could not play this anymore. I probably have even more hours on that copy, but that's only because I cannot play this one! Downvoting because disappointed in devs for doing this to a large portion of their player base. Still hoping I'll be able to come back to this someday; maybe after I upgrade to a different VR headset.  If you are able to play it, its a great time! 8.5/10

This game is unbelievably fun. The guns are very crisp and excellent to work with. Each gun has its own particular way of reloading as well as learnable recoil pattern very similar to Counter Strike. In fact, this game is very much similar to CSGo/CS2 in VR and even has a large amount of CS maps ported over. This game has a VR Esport community around this idea, while the community is smaller now due to other games taking player counts over the years and lack of updates in the past. I think the real downfall of this game is the loss of years and years of previous passionate players mods when Pav switched to the new Unreal Engine. Still, theres so much to find and do, and this game is a thrill to try to get good at. It even has PS5 Crossover.

Admittedly the game looks among the BEST in VR with only HLA really being a better contender. But in regards to tight realistic and short TTK gritty VR gameplay, this is as good as it gets. 

Lots of maps, lots of modes, so much to try and master. 
From:
Cod Zombies mods, TTT, Prophunt, BAttlefield like modes with rush on vietnam/WW2/Modern, Vehicles in some modes like tanks and helicopters, TDM, DM, CSGo bomb like mode: (SND), There are infection modes of various sorts, Tarkovlike modes, PubZ like modes, I think even more  - really the possibilities are only limited to the mods and the player counts in a game like this.


I have a lot of time and history with this game, and will always love the community, the game, the developers, and even where the game is now. 

But,
After the big UE5 Update, so much feels missing. Even though the modding tools are better than they were before, knowing how much was lost hurts a lot. Especially as some of my favorite VR experinces like FNAF2 VR, CODZombies Origins, Some RP Servers, are just - gone. For me, i felt like i experinced the Golden Years of Pavlov during Covid and beyond, and some of the best days in Esports for the game in the VRML (look em up!)

I think i will play this game even w…

Pavlov kind of fell off.

I first got my PCVR headset in 2018ish, and Pavlov was *the* VR game to get (outside of Beat Saber haha). It hits that perfect balance between adhering to some sense of realism, and allowing for arcadey action, where Counter-Strike tends to sit. A big draw for me was the Steam Workshop support, most of the time when other people are playing, you head to the server browser and see a large variety of maps and gamemodes available to choose from. A particular favorite of mine was always the Jailbreak gamemode/map, you have a team of jail guards looking after the other team of prisors, whose goal is to do the jailbreaking mentioned in the gamemodes title. It was always a thrill dashing around the map as a prisoner, doing various tasks to enable my escape, under watchful eye of guards who are most likely going to RDM me.

Anywho, Vankrupt Games made the highly logical move of making a Meta Quest version of the game available to players, with the unfortunate compromise of not supporting the Steam Workshop, which really isn't there fault, how would the infrastructure of pushing Steam Workshop content to a non-Steam game even work? Most of the submissions would not even be optimized for running on the mobile device. This effectively killed a lot of activity on Steam Workshop maps, as a significant portion of the playerbase are unable to access to content, most who can just end up joining those who cannot because they have the most players. Again, this isn't Vankrupts Games fault, it's just unfortunate circumstances from my perspective.

Another issue with making the game more accessible is how it effects who is in the playerbase, there's just a lot more young children in lobbies which really throws off the vibe I got prior to the Meta Quest version of the game. Again, not Vankrupt Games fault.

I love Pavlov VR, the guns are constantly fascinating to hold and manipulate, they're fun to try to shoot others with, and I still have lots of fun with the …

Reasons for the Decline in PC Player Count
Broken Mod Support: A significant factor was the shift from the highly popular and easy-to-use Steam Workshop to the less intuitive Mod.io platform as part of a major engine upgrade (to Unreal Engine 5). This change made it difficult for content creators to port or develop new maps and mods (such as popular Call of Duty zombie maps), which had previously been a major draw for the game.
Developer Focus on Console: Many PC players feel the developers, Vankrupt Games, abandoned the PC version to focus on the more lucrative Quest and PSVR2 platforms. The PC version allegedly lagged in features for a long time, leading to player frustration.
Technical Issues and Performance: The engine upgrade itself caused numerous problems for PC players, including performance drops, input issues, and controller problems, some of which were never adequately addressed for all users. The game became harder to run for some players, prompting them to leave.
Gameplay Changes: The update also introduced unwanted gameplay changes, such as a forced HUD showing teammate locations through walls, which altered the tactical flow of popular modes like "Push" and "Search and Destroy".
Competition: Due to these issues, many players migrated to alternative VR shooters like Contractors or Ghosts of Tabor, which maintained better mod support or offered a more stable experience.    TY for killing…
